summary: The gaia variant is a design plus code submission with a GAIA PDF, README, and a SPADE-based Python prototype. It covers container fill monitoring and basic container-to-dispatch notification, but the implementation does not actually choose the nearest truck, does not enforce the one-day deadline, and does not prioritize more-filled trucks. The code also contains hardcoded SPADE credentials, which is a critical security finding under the judge rubric.

findings.description: The system explicitly models smart containers and sends a notification when a container reaches the fill threshold.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:34-43 checks fill_level >= 90 and sends Message(to="dispatch_system@localhost") with ContainerID, FillLevel, and Timestamp.

findings.description: The nearest-truck requirement is not implemented; the dispatcher returns the first available truck without any location or distance calculation.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:138-142: find_nearest_available_truck iterates self.agent.trucks and returns the first truck whose Status is Available.

findings.description: The one-day collection requirement is only stored as a deadline timestamp and is never enforced by a follow-up action, escalation, or reassignment.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:112-117 stores Deadline = datetime.now() + timedelta(days=1); ContainerStatusMonitor at lines 145-148 only sleeps and contains a placeholder comment.

findings.description: The requirement to prioritize more-filled garbage trucks is absent from the dispatch algorithm.
findings.evidence: gaia/Seroidtest.pdf page 2 lists DispatchSystem responsibilities including PrioritizeGarbageTrucks, but gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:138-142 checks only Status == "Available".

findings.description: Truck assignment messages are addressed to truck IDs rather than the actual truck JIDs, making assignment delivery inconsistent with the created agents.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:126 sends to f"{nearest_truck}@localhost" while truck agents are created as "truck1@localhost" and "truck2@localhost" at lines 164-165 and registered under IDs "T001" and "T002" at lines 178-179.

findings.description: SPADE agent passwords are hardcoded in source.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:160-167 creates agents with literal passwords "password1" through "password6".

findings.description: Debug-style print statements are used throughout runtime paths instead of structured logging.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py includes print calls in agent setup and message handling, including lines 19, 44, 58, 69, 110, 134, 157, 181, and 194.

missing_requirements: Actual nearest non-full garbage truck selection based on distance or location.
Operational enforcement that a full container is not left full for more than one day.
Prioritization of more-filled garbage trucks during assignment.
Reliable monitoring of full truck state; implemented statuses use Available, Busy, and Maintenance, while the requirement needs busy, full, and free.
logical_inconsistencies: The README claims automatic nearest available garbage truck assignment, but the code returns the first available truck without distance data.

The GAIA design includes DispatchSystemToGarbageTruckStatusUpdate and DispatchSystemToGarbageTruckPriorityAssignment protocols, but the implementation only handles DispatchSystemToGarbageTruckAssignment.
Truck identifiers are mixed: assignment messages use T001/T002 as JIDs, while the actual SPADE agents are truck1@localhost and truck2@localhost.
implementation_risks: Assignments may never reach truck agents because message recipient JIDs do not match created truck agent JIDs.
Hardcoded credentials make deployment unsafe and environment-specific.
Full containers can remain overdue because deadline enforcement is not implemented.
Dispatch decisions can overload or underuse trucks because truck load and distance are not considered.
